articles.title: Margherita Ferrari on Working With Paolo Sorrentino on Directorial Debut ‘Föa — Once Upon a Future’: ‘He Helped Me Pursue and Protect My Vision’
articles.summary: Debuting Italian director Margherita Ferrari is at the Busan International Film Festival with “Föa – Once Upon a Future,” an innovative coming-of-age drama that also marks Paolo Sorrentino’s debut as a producer.
body: The film, bowing at Busan Film Festival, is set in Genoa in July 2001 when the G8 summit led to deathly clashes.

“Föa – Once Upon a Future,” which stars emerging talents Gaia Ravina, Clara Tramontano, Iker Urgoiti and Gabriele Falsetta, was co-produced by Sorrentino′s production company Numero 10, with The Apartment and PiperFilm. PiperPlay is handling international sales.

“At a time when imagination needs to be protected, supporting new authors and their singular visions feels more important than ever,” Sorrentino continued. “I am particularly proud that Numero 10 begins this journey with a film told through such a powerful female gaze — a story that reminds us that even after the future seems to have disappeared, it may still be waiting for us.”

The film started as Ferrari’s graduation short at Rome’s Centro Sperimentale film school, after which she had the opportunity to pitch the expanded project to Sorrentino. Below, Ferrari speaks to Variety about what sparked “Once Upon a Future” creatively and its fortuitous production journey.

articles.title: UTA and Gold House Set Partnership to Build Asia-Hollywood Bridge (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: UTA and Gold House are joining forces at the Busan International Film Festival and in Seoul this month, marking the Asian Pacific advocacy organization’s first official foray into Korea as the two look to connect Asian creatives and investors with Hollywood.
body: Until now, Gold House’s formal footprint in Asia had been limited to Singapore and Taiwan. Christine Yi, executive VP and president, Gold House Studios., is of Korean heritage, as is Daniel Suh, who runs the organization’s venture capital fund. The pair made an exploratory trip to Korea around this time last year to meet people in the local industry and ask what role Gold House could play.

“What we had heard the most about was, do the Gold House thing here. You don’t really have to reinvent the wheel,” Yi says. “Especially as it relates to bringing major Hollywood executives, Dave included, to the table in order to really help facilitate more cross-border partnership, that’s something that they would really want from us.”

“I don’t know if 2026 is the right moment, honestly. The right moment would have been sometime in the past, so I would say that we’re actually overdue,” Yi adds, pointing to Gold House’s investments in Korean startups and the number of its investors based in the country.

articles.title: A Rare David Bowie Self-Portrait — Featuring His Handprints — Is Going on Auction at Sotheby’s
articles.summary: A rare David Bowie self-portrait is going on auction at Sotheby’s, featuring the musician and artist’s own handprints. The 1996 work is part of eight self-portraits Bowie created during a prolific period of painting, all of which were snapped up immediately.
body: “There’s something incredibly direct and personal about this self-portrait,” Jen Hardie, Sotheby’s director and senior specialist of modern British and Irish art, tells Variety. “Bowie looks straight out at you, and his own handprints appear on the work itself. It’s bold, colorful and unmistakably Bowie, capturing the same restless creativity that ran through everything he did. It also feels particularly special to see a work like this return to Sotheby’s, a decade after our landmark ‘Bowie/Collector’ sale celebrated the extraordinary breadth of his own collection.”

Indeed, “Bowie/Collector” in 2016 sold more than 350 works from Bowie’s private collection, bringing in £32.9 million ($43.4 million) and setting 59 artist records. Bowie was an admirer or German Expressionism, dating back to his years in Berlin in the ’70s, and also of School of London artists Leon Kossoff and Frank Auerbach — the influences of which can all be seen in his own work.

articles.title: Crazy Rich Asians TV show to reunite Constance Wu and Henry Golding
articles.summary: The show will pick up after the hit 2018 film, and will also star Michelle Yeoh and Ronny Chieng.
body: Four of the stars of 2018's Crazy Rich Asians film are reprising their roles for a TV show of the same name.

The series will pick up events after the end of the hit film, with Constance Wu and Henry Golding playing their lead roles of Rachel and Nick, while Ronny Chieng is back as Eddie and Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh will have a recurring role as Nick's mother Eleanor.

"It's a 'Crazy Rich' family reunion!" said Adele Lim, who co-wrote the film, calling it the sequel we've been waiting for". It will "delve into the characters and worlds of Kevin Kwan's brilliant books" over eight episodes, she said.
The show will be made by HBO, and the news was announced days after HBO's parent company Warner Bros announced its £110bn (£82.8bn) merger with Paramount Skydance.

articles.title: Alison Hammond: 'I thought I was having heart attack on air'
articles.summary: The host says a health scare was "probably one of the most scariest things I've ever been through".
body: Alison Hammond has said she feared she was having a heart attack on air when she had to rush off ITV's This Morning, mid-way through the programme last week.
The presenter appeared to clutch her chest as she left the show last Friday, and was taken to hospital to have a heart check-up.
She told viewers: "I couldn't catch my breath and I genuinely thought I was having a heart attack. I'm so glad I'm here. I feel so grateful. I feel so thankful to God, to everything in life."
Alongside co-host Dermot O'Leary, Hammond introduced the programme by thanking him for holding the fort after her dramatic early exit, and thanking everyone who sent good wishes.

articles.title: ‘Old-timey fascism was kept secret. Now you don’t have to hide it’: Martin McDonagh, John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell on Wild Horse Nine
articles.summary: McDonagh’s latest film has Malkovich and Rockwell shooting the breeze as CIA agents in 1973 on Easter Island. They discuss grandchildren, swimming with turtles and who shot JFK. ‘Earmuffs!” says Sam Rockwell, pausing his gushing tribute mid-flow and turning to face John Malkovich on the couch.
body: In Martin McDonagh’s Wild Horse Nine, Malkovich and Rockwell play bickering CIA agents who may also be the best of friends. Chris and Lee are fresh from plotting the 1973 coup in Chile and are spinning their wheels on Rapa Nui, amid the crashing waves and the moai statues. They’ve seen too much and sinned too greatly and now Chris has cancer, which is hardly helping his mood. So he takes Lee aside and asks for one last big favour. “Shoot me in the head on Easter Island,” he says.

Ahead of the film’s premiere, the production team commandeer suites at an opulent Venice hotel and hand out hats and T-shirts to each new arrival. The lobby becomes a sea of merch. The harried concierge has to raise his voice to be heard. He says: “Second floor for the Six White Horses press interviews.”

body: A live-action movie version of smash hit video game Cyberpunk 2077 is being developed by Paramount Pictures.
The Hollywood studio is working with producer Lorenzo di Bonaventura, known for his work on the Transformers films, and CD Projekt Red (CDPR), the developer of the sci-fi role-playing game.

CDPR's joint-chief executive Michał Nowakowski said in a statement, external the company was "excited about Paramount as a future partner who shares our creative ambitions for the Cyberpunk franchise".
Details of the film's story, potential release date and casting information are yet to be revealed.

articles.title: Music group with learning difficulties fulfils late MP's Broadway dream
articles.summary: The Music Man Project is a charity in Essex that teaches music to people with learning disabilities.
body: A music group with learning disabilities received a standing ovation as they fulfilled a dream of the late MP Sir David Amess.
The Music Man Project is a charity based in Southend-on-Sea, Essex, that teaches children and adults with learning disabilities to sing, sign and play original music.

They have performed for the King, at the Royal Albert Hall and London Palladium, but a trip to perform in New York was the dream of their former president and Southend West MP Amess before he was murdered in 2021.
The project's founder David Stanley said: "Following his death, I just made it my mission to fulfil that promise, really, in his memory."

articles.title: Skydance’s Gerhard Zeiler, Warner Bros. Int’l President, to Depart With Eyes on Politics
articles.summary: "It is surprisingly difficult to find the right words to say goodbye," the Austrian writes in an internal memo obtained by The Hollywood Reporter. "At the end of next week, I will leave the company."
body: David Ellison ‘s merged Paramount-Warner Bros., now known as Skydance, is going through all sorts of executive changes now that the mega-combination is complete. Gerhard Zeiler, who has been serving as president, international for Warner Bros. Discovery, is the latest executive to leave – and he may be eyeing a new career in Austrian politics.

His memo didn’t mention any successor for him in his role, but the recently unveiled Skydance management ranks all feature execs with global responsibility. For example, JB Perrette has been tapped as co-chair and chief business officer of Skydance TV and Skydance DTC, effectively giving him global oversight of the business of TV and streaming.

Zeiler was appointed president of WarnerMedia International in 2020, adding responsibility for Discovery’s international footprint following the close of the Discovery-WarnerMedia merger in April 2022. He first joined Turner in 2012 as president, Turner International, where he oversaw the entertainment and kids’ networks in all markets outside of North America.

articles.title: Sofia Coppola Plans Return to Narrative Film, But Has Her Late Mother’s ‘Making Marie Antoinette’ to See Off First
articles.summary: The filmmaker spoke tenderly about seeing herself "through her mother's eyes" in the documentary, though recalled about lead star Kirsten Dunst: "At the time, people didn't like her performance."
body: Sofia Coppola spoke tenderly about her late mother and their family’s film legacy at a BFI London Film Festival session on Thursday afternoon.

Her answer? A deliciously vibrant, sugary take on the ill-fated 18th-century Queen of France with Kirsten Dunst in the titular role. Eleanor Coppola — who had Sofia with fellow filmmaker Francis Ford Coppola in 1971 — turned the camera on her daughter and captured over 80 hours of behind-the-scenes and on-set action while musing on what it means for a mother to watch her 34-year-old daughter at work. The documentary Making Marie Antoinette, assembled by Sofia Coppola and editor Aaron Matthews with input from Eleanor’s close friends, is screening here at the 70th London Film Festival, two-and-a-half years after Coppola’s death.
